bacterial spot.description: Bacterial spot appears as small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit, which may later become scabby.
bacterial spot.cause: Bacterial pathogens such as Xanthomonas spp.
treatment: Prune and remove infected plant parts to prevent spread.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds or transplants.
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness.
Practice crop rotation.
fertilizer_recommendation: Maintain a balanced fertilizer program to support plant health and resilience.
Typical application: 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus (P2O5), and 200-250 kg Potassium (K2O) per hectare.

early blight.description: Early blight is characterized by dark brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves, leading to premature defoliation.
treatment: Apply fungicides such as mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or azoxystrobin.
Remove severely infected leaves and plant debris.
prevention: Plant resistant tomato varieties.
Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead watering.
Rotate crops to reduce fungal inoculum.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.
Adequate potassium can enhance disease resistance.
soil_recommendation: Best grown in well-drained, fertile loamy soils.

healthy.description: A healthy tomato plant has vibrant green leaves, strong stems, and is free of any disease symptoms or pests.
treatment: Follow a regular watering and fertilization schedule.
Regularly monitor plants for early signs of disease or pests.
prevention: Use certified seeds and resistant varieties.
Maintain good field sanitation.
Practice crop rotation to prevent soil-borne diseases.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.
Split nitrogen applications for optimal growth.
soil_recommendation: Well-drained, fertile loam soil is ideal.

late blight.description: Late blight causes large, irregular, water-soaked spots on leaves and stems that quickly turn black. Fruit develop dark, sunken lesions.
treatment: Spray systemic fungicides like metalaxyl or cymoxanil combined with protectants like mancozeb.
Destroy heavily infected plants to limit disease spread.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties.
Ensure proper plant spacing for good air circulation.
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness by managing irrigation.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.
Higher potassium levels can improve tolerance to late blight.
soil_recommendation: Avoid excess irrigation to reduce humidity.

leaf mold.description: Leaf mold presents as pale green or yellow spots on the top leaf surface with a velvety, olive-green to brown mold on the underside.
treatment: Use fungicides such as chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin.
Increase air circulation and reduce humidity in the growing area.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties.
Ensure proper ventilation, especially in greenhouses.
Avoid overhead watering.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.

mosaic virus.description: This virus causes a mottled, mosaic-like pattern of light and dark green on leaves, leading to stunted growth and reduced fruit yield.
treatment: Immediately remove and destroy infected plants.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and transplants.
Avoid using tobacco products around the plants, as the virus can be transmitted by smokers.
Disinfect tools and hands regularly.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.
A balanced diet helps plants cope with viral stress.
soil_recommendation: Grows best in well-drained, fertile soil.

septoria spot.description: Septoria leaf spot causes small, circular spots with dark borders and gray or tan centers, often with tiny black specks in the middle.
treatment: Apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
Remove and destroy affected lower leaves.
prevention: Practice good field sanitation by removing plant debris.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Rotate crops to a non-host plant.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.

yellow leafCurl.description: Leaves curl upward, become crinkled and leathery. Plants are severely stunted, and flowers may drop without producing fruit.
yellow leafCurl.cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), transmitted by whiteflies.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
prevention: Use resistant or tolerant tomato varieties.
Control whitefly populations using insecticides or sticky traps.
Use insect-proof nets in greenhouses.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150-200 kg Nitrogen, 80-100 kg Phosphorus, and 200-250 kg Potassium per hectare.
A balanced fertilizer program supports plant growth.
